description:
The arm that licenses reading anything else. Phase one is byte-identical to `symmetric_rivals`; phase two delivers one observation that only one reading can accommodate.

A state that cannot break is a state we wrote. Requirements section 2 flavour A, and the reason this fixture exists: without it, 'the meta-belief held' is not evidence of anything at all. Pre-registration section 2 fixes what counts - a fall of at least 0.15 from the `symmetric_rivals` value, and strictly further than on `near_miss`.

The fall must come through the ordinary confidence pathway. `BeliefUpdater._revise` only moves a belief when the candidate brings evidence it does not already hold, so the separating record arriving on `reading_a` is disconfirming evidence for the meta-belief in exactly the way any other evidence would be. If a bespoke rule is needed to make this collapse, FR-2 has been violated and the finding is that we wrote an exemption.

expect.note: Structural. The separating record is held by `reading_a` and not by `reading_b`, so the symmetric difference of their evidence sets is non-empty in phase 2 and empty in phase 1. What the criterion and the meta-belief's confidence do about that is computed, not declared.

evidence.summary: The distant supernovae are dimmer than a static model predicts.
The dimming is the same in every direction we have measured.

beliefs.proposition: The dimming is best explained by a change in expansion over time.
The dimming is best explained by our position within a large underdense region.
